subtopic: Dealing with bureaucracy and corruption pressure
passage:
Anand, twenty-four, was the newest clerk in the ward office. On Tuesday Divyansh, a senior colleague, put a hand on his shoulder. "Here we share the extras. Everybody chips in, everybody's safe." Anand said quietly that he would manage without.
By Friday nobody asked him to tea. Files piled onto his desk, and lunch was eaten in silence in the corner. He felt like a stranger in his own section.
The section officer called him in. "Keep every file note dated. If anyone pushes again, write it down and give it to me. I will send it to the vigilance cell." That afternoon she forwarded his note, and the cell acknowledged it within the day. Anand still felt lonely, but less afraid.

qa.q: What was Anand feeling during the week after he said he would manage without?
qa.a: He felt lonely and like a stranger, with nobody asking him to tea and lunch eaten in silence.

qa.q: What made the difference in protecting Anand?
qa.a: The section officer told him to keep dated file notes, took his written note and forwarded it to the vigilance cell that afternoon, so a clear rule and a legal channel backed him.

qa.q: How might Divyansh have seen Anand's refusal?
qa.a: Divyansh may have felt uneasy or threatened, since he had called it a way everybody stays safe, and Anand's refusal broke that shared arrangement.

grounding: A young government employee is pushed to join a shared arrangement of favours, and refusing brings isolation but a mentor and legal channels protect them.

passage:
"You didn't come to the tea corner again," said Seema, setting her tray down opposite Kiran.
"I'm not in the mood."
"Because of the monthly 'collection' for the supervisor?"
Kiran looked at the table. "He said everyone contributes. I said no. Now I've been dropped from the office group and nobody speaks to me."
"That's how it starts. You did right, Kiran."
"Doesn't feel right. Feels lonely."
"It is lonely for a while. Write what was said, when and by whom. Dated. Then we take it to the chief this afternoon."
That evening Seema came back to Kiran's desk. "The chief has called the supervisor in, and the anti-corruption cell has your note. You sit with me for lunch from tomorrow."
Kiran nodded, throat tight.

qa.q: Where did Seema sit when she joined Kiran?
qa.a: Seema set her tray down opposite Kiran.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling after refusing the monthly 'collection'?
qa.a: Kiran felt lonely and shut out, since the office group dropped Kiran and nobody spoke.

qa.q: What steps did Seema take that protected Kiran?
qa.a: Seema told Kiran to write down what was said, when and by whom, took the note to the chief that afternoon, and the chief called in the supervisor and the anti-corruption cell had the note.

qa.q: What is it like for Seema to see Kiran isolated?
qa.a: Seema seems to know this pattern and to feel protective, saying 'That's how it starts' and inviting Kiran to sit with Seema for lunch.

grounding: A young government employee refuses a shared arrangement of favours, faces isolation, and is protected by an honest mentor and proper channels.
